subject: Art & Design
title: Sound Branding: The Audio Logo
description: A quick win: understand Sound Branding: The Audio Logo.

hook.text: You hear five notes and think Intel. Three seconds of audio can be as recognizable as any visual logo.

buildup.text: Sound branding creates audio identities: jingles, sonic logos, and brand sounds that trigger instant recognition.

discovery.text: Netflix's 'ta-dum' was designed to feel like a deep breath before a movie. It cost nothing but is worth billions.

twist.text: Most brands invest millions in visual identity but ignore sound. In podcasts and voice assistants, silence is a risk.

climax.text: Mastercard created a full sonic identity: a melody adapted across genres and cultures but always recognizable.

punchline.text: A brand you can hear is a brand you can't forget.

quiz.question: What is a sonic logo?
options: A short audio signature that identifies a brand instantly
A logo designed using sound wave imagery

details.summary: An audio logo (sonic logo) is a brief, distinctive sound or melody that identifies a brand — like the NBC chimes (three notes since 1927), the THX Deep Note, or Apple's startup chime. Audio logos must work across different contexts — from TV commercials to elevator speakers to phone notifications.
details.whyItMatters: Audio logos are among the most sticky brand elements because music activates memory circuits more powerfully than visual images. A well-designed audio logo can trigger brand recall years after last hearing it.
takeaways: A 2-5 second sound or melody identifies the brand instantly
NBC's three-note chime has been used since 1927
Music activates memory more powerfully than visual images

faq.question: How long should an audio logo be?
faq.answer: Typically 1-5 seconds. Intel's is about 3 seconds, Netflix's ta-dum is about 2 seconds. Brevity is essential — the sound must work in fast-paced media transitions. Longer musical pieces serve as brand anthems rather than logos, providing a broader musical identity.

faq.question: Can audio logos be trademarked?
faq.answer: Yes. The NBC chimes were among the first sounds trademarked in the US (1950). Intel, Nokia, T-Mobile, and others have registered their sonic logos. Trademark law requires the sound to be distinctive and consistently used in commerce, just like visual trademarks.
